headline: Semiconductors Steer Tuesday's Rally as Breadth Tilts Positive
body_html:
Midway through Tuesday's session, equities are holding a constructive tone, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by a margin of 330 to 215 across the 549-name universe. Semiconductors are setting the pace, gaining 1.8% as a group and pulling Materials (+0.96%) and Industrials (+0.61%) higher in their wake. Energy and Homebuilders are also trading in positive territory, suggesting the rally has some width beyond pure technology.

The standout mover of the session is SolarEdge, up nearly 5% and leading all gainers in the broader tech-adjacent space. Semiconductor equipment names are clustered directly behind it — Onto Innovation, FormFactor, and Teradyne are each adding more than 4% — reinforcing the chip-hardware bid that is driving the day's sector narrative. PDF Solutions and Jabil round out the top performers, adding further texture to the manufacturing and semi-supply-chain theme.

On the downside, AECOM is the session's most jarring outlier, off nearly 12% and standing well apart from any other decliner. Software is the only sector registering a meaningful loss at -0.51%, with Datadog sliding 4.7%. Into the close, watch whether Software stabilizes and whether AECOM's drop broadens into the wider Industrials complex, which for now remains in the green.

briefs.headline: Chip-Equipment Names Stage Broad Midday Surge
briefs.body: Onto Innovation, FormFactor, and Teradyne are each advancing more than 4% through the midday hour, reflecting coordinated buying across semiconductor test and process-control equipment. The cluster of gains suggests institutional rotation into the hardware layer of the chip supply chain rather than isolated, stock-specific news.

briefs.headline: AECOM Slumps Nearly 12%, Worst Decline in the Universe
briefs.body: Engineering and infrastructure services firm AECOM is the session's most notable casualty, shedding close to 12% and sitting far below the next-worst decliner. The severity of the move stands in contrast to Industrials as a sector, which remains modestly positive on the day, implying the pressure is company-specific rather than macro-driven.

briefs.headline: SolarEdge Leads All Gainers With Nearly 5% Advance
briefs.body: SolarEdge is atop the leaderboard through midday, climbing just under 5% and making it the most actively appreciated name across the broader universe. The solar-technology firm's outperformance adds an energy-transition layer to what is otherwise a semiconductor-dominated leadership picture.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Slides as Datadog Weighs on the Group
briefs.body: Software is the weakest sector midway through Tuesday's session, off 0.51%, with Datadog accounting for a large share of that drag at -4.68%. The divergence between Software's weakness and Semiconductors' strength underscores a rotation within technology toward hardware-centric names today.

briefs.headline: Consumer Names Soften; Dick's Sporting Goods and Deckers Both Retreat
briefs.body: Dick's Sporting Goods is off 3.76% and Deckers Brands is down 3.33%, pressuring the Consumer sector to a -0.41% reading at midday. The back-to-back declines in sporting and footwear retail point to selective selling in discretionary names even as the broader tape holds a positive tilt.

briefs.headline: Market Breadth Favors Bulls by a 60-40 Margin at Midday
briefs.body: With 330 advancers against 215 decliners out of 549 names, Tuesday's session is displaying healthy if not emphatic breadth. Six of eight tracked sectors are in positive territory, and the split suggests the rally has enough participation to avoid being dismissed as a narrow, momentum-driven move into the afternoon hours.
